purpose: The build standard the legacy flows already follow, written down. Derived from the 57 deployed definitions rather than invented - every rule below is something a majority of the estate already does, and the counts are in the conformance report.
provenance: Read out of docs/folio-Master-Flows-and-Endpoints/contracts/deployed/ on 2026-08-19. scripts/verify-flow-standard.mjs measures conformance; it does not enforce it, because a standard applied retroactively as a gate turns every legacy flow red on the day it is written.

checks.title: Standard variable set initialised
checks.why: Every flow reports its outcome through the same three variables, which is what lets one response envelope serve all of them.

checks.title: Timing variables initialised
checks.why: The envelope and the run record both report timing; computing it once at the top is what keeps them agreeing.

checks.title: Scope_Global wraps the work
checks.why: One scope to attach a catch to. Without it the failure path has to be repeated on every branch.

checks.title: A catch scope on runAfter Failed
checks.why: An HTTP-triggered flow that faults without a catch returns a platform error page to the caller instead of the envelope.
checks.detect: any Scope action whose runAfter includes Failed, whatever it is named

checks.title: The standard response envelope
checks.why: ok, status{http,code,message}, request{...}, timing{...}, data, errors, meta. core/contracts.js unwraps exactly this shape; a flow answering any other shape has to be special-cased in the client.

checks.title: A Response action returns it
checks.why: A request-triggered flow that never responds leaves the caller waiting for its timeout.

checks.title: Scope_Flow_Data_Capture
checks.why: The observability harness: a versioned run record with its own JSON Schema, the trigger schema, the full definition and the response, captured on every run.

checks.title: A versioned flow_run_record is composed
checks.why: capture_version 2.0.0, with capture_metadata, workflow_identity, run_identity, trigger_record, request, design_definition, response_record, outcome and timing.

checks.title: Headers redacted before capture
checks.why: Authorization, Cookie, x-api-key and Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key are blanked before the request is recorded. Without it the telemetry becomes the leak.

checks.title: Query string redacted before capture
checks.why: sig and code are blanked. sig is the trigger credential; code is the one-time password. This estate got that right before anything else did.

responseEnvelope.note: Collections may also appear at the top level beside data - Fetch_Tasks returns tasks, and core/data-loader.js reads a collection by alias. Adding one is within the standard; replacing the envelope is not.

redaction.note: This is stricter than the repository-side redaction in scripts/redact-signed-urls.ps1, which did not cover code. Aligned in that script rather than left divergent.

telemetrySink.portalFlows: Create_Flow_Telemetry inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture writes one row per run to Portal Flow Telemetry (Global_Digital_Documents_Centre, 726c210d-09d5-45d9-952d-7a506b644b13), per DECISIONS.md D2 as revised 2026-08-19.
telemetrySink.legacy: Send_Telemetry_Email ships the four attachments. That is how every definition in docs/reference/foundational/flows/definitions/ came to exist - they are captured attachments, and their filenames are this convention. Email is not queryable, which is what Portal Flow Telemetry was provisioned to fix.

scope.catch.title: Add a catch scope
scope.catch.how: Add a Scope named Scope_<Purpose>_Catch as a peer of the work scope, then set its 'Configure run after' to Failed, Skipped and Timed out - all three, not just Failed.
scope.catch.why: An HTTP-triggered flow that faults without a catch returns a platform error page to the caller instead of the envelope. On a public endpoint that page is also an information disclosure.

redaction.headers.title: Redact headers before capture
redaction.headers.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Headers, running after Compose_Redacted_Queries.
redaction.headers.why: Without it the observability harness becomes the leak.

wireInto.note: Same: an unconsumed Compose redacts nothing. Compose_Flow_Run_Record must also be moved to run after Compose_Redacted_Headers, or it composes before the value exists.

redaction.queries.title: Redact the query string before capture
redaction.queries.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Redacted_Queries. Place it first in that scope, immediately after Get_Flow_Definition.
redaction.queries.why: sig is the trigger credential and code is the one-time password. On the verification flows this is the difference between telemetry and a log of every OTP issued.

wireInto.note: Adding the Compose without this leaves it inert: the run record captures no query string at all, and the conformance check still passes. The rule is about what reaches telemetry, not about an action existing.

vars.timing.title: Initialise the timing variables
vars.timing.how: Four more Initialize variable actions, alongside the core set.

alsoAdd.name: Scope_Finalize_Response_State
alsoAdd.where: Inside Scope_Global, after the work and before the envelope

vars.timing.why: The envelope and the run record both report timing. Computing it once is what keeps them agreeing.

scope.global.title: Wrap the work in Scope_Global
scope.global.how: Add a Scope named Scope_Global and move every existing action except the Initialize variable actions inside it.
scope.global.why: One place to attach a catch. Without it the failure path has to be repeated on every branch, which is why the flows missing this are the same flows missing a catch.

telemetry.capture.title: Add Scope_Flow_Data_Capture
telemetry.capture.how: Add a Scope named Scope_Flow_Data_Capture as a top-level peer of Scope_Global, with 'Configure run after' set to Succeeded, Failed, Skipped and Timed out - it must run whatever happened.
telemetry.capture.why: The observability harness twenty-three flows already carry. Adding it is what makes this flow visible in the same way as the rest of the estate.

telemetry.record.title: Compose the versioned run record
telemetry.record.how: Inside Scope_Flow_Data_Capture, add a Compose named Compose_Flow_Run_Record.
telemetry.record.copyFrom: Any conforming flow - Fetch_Tasks_POST is the cleanest. Copy Compose_Flow_Run_Record verbatim; it reads only workflow(), trigger(), the redaction composes and the standard variables, so it is portable between flows unchanged.
telemetry.record.why: capture_version 2.0.0, with its draft-07 schema alongside. Copying rather than rewriting is the point - a second dialect of the record is worse than none.

vars.core.title: Initialise the standard variable set
vars.core.how: Three Initialize variable actions at the very top of the flow, before Scope_Global.
vars.core.why: One response envelope can only serve every flow if every flow reports its outcome the same way.

response.envelope.title: Answer through the standard envelope
response.envelope.how: Add a Compose named Compose__Standard_Response_Revised as the last action inside Scope_Global, before the Response.
response.envelope.why: core/contracts.js unwraps exactly this shape. A flow answering anything else has to be special-cased in the client, which is how one-off shapes accumulate.

response.action.title: Return the envelope
response.action.how: Add a Response action as the last action inside Scope_Global.
response.action.why: A request-triggered flow that never responds leaves the caller waiting for its timeout.
